comments.body:
OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-07): the fallback chain stays OFF until this ticket lands — AND this ticket is committed to, not deferred.

The operator challenged my framing of the options, correctly. I had offered 'leave it off' and 'fix first, then enable' as separate choices; they are the same choice, differing only in whether this ticket is scheduled. There is no argument for leaving the underlying defect unfixed, so it is scheduled.

The defect, restated so it stands alone: when two models are configured as a chain, the runner INTERSECTS capabilities across candidates (runner.py:441). us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 is measured native-structured-output-capable (ticket 18ae) while its direct-Anthropic twin deliberately stays PromptedOutput. So configuring the chain silently moves EVERY standard-class call project-wide from native to prompted structured output — a measured decision undone as a side effect of an unrelated resilience setting. test_provider_parity.py catches it and was deliberately left catching it rather than relaxed.

Worth fixing regardless of whether the Anthropic fallback is ever enabled: capability intersection means ANY future chain — a second Bedrock region, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a cheaper model for a low-stakes class — pays the same silent tax. The resilience feature is currently unusable without a capability regression, which is a defect in the CHAIN MECHANISM, not in the choice of fallback provider.

Direction for whoever implements: the up-front intersection is the wrong default. A chain should not degrade the PRIMARY's capabilities to match a fallback that may never be invoked; capability should be resolved per-attempt against the model actually being called. The real design question — answer it explicitly rather than by intersecting defensively — is what happens when a fallback attempt cannot honour a request shape the primary already accepted.

Related, and NOT resolved by this ticket: the direct-Anthropic arm is currently unreachable in non-interactive contexts for a separate reason — a valid key exists in ~/.zshrc but an INVALID one shadows it in the process environment agents and gates run in. See the credential-shadowing diagnosis recorded on 2876 (interactive key -> HTTP 200, non-interactive -> HTTP 401, different hashes, same length). Enabling the chain before that is fixed would exercise an invalid credential.

comments.body:
## rebar-debug Phase 1 — mechanism proven; legitimacy: intended-behavior / approved superseding design

No production defect in the existing chain mechanism was found. The observed downgrade is the exact behavior deliberately specified by the original fallback feature, while the requested per-attempt behavior is a later, operator-approved redesign. No Phase 2 bug repair is unlocked by this classification.

### Confirmed mechanism

1. **No fallback currently runs.** The live `rebar.toml` has no `fallback` entry, and the real config lookup returns `fallback_targets_for("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", repo_root=".") == ()`. This is the immediate reason the approved direct arm is not exercised.
2. **Configuring the arm alone deterministically selects PromptedOutput before any attempt.** With the proposed standard slot supplied through the real class parser, runtime values were: candidates `[bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6]`; per-candidate native flags `[(True, True), (False, False)]`; `_intersect_capabilities` produced `(False, False)`; `structured.output_mode` returned `PromptedOutput` both with and without thinking. The executing path is `runner.py:427-433` -> `_intersect_capabilities` (`runner.py:727-753`) -> `_pai_structured` / `output_mode` (`structured_run.py:186-215`, `structured.py:219+`).
3. **That up-front collapse is intentional, not an implementation accident.** Original task `worthless-titanite-bubblefish` explicitly decided that capabilities are a conservative intersection computed before the wrapper and requires the whole-chain temperature-withdrawal test. Its tests execute the rule: the restricted candidate withdraws temperature for the entire chain, the all-capable negative control retains it, and capabilities are resolved per candidate rather than from the wrapper (3 focused tests PASS). Story `bixbite-sealbrown-kinkajou` separately requires an all-capable chain to preserve native-under-thinking and a mixed chain to collapse to false; it explicitly records direct Anthropic as unmeasured/fail-closed.
4. **The wrapper cannot switch output shape per attempt by itself.** A runtime `FallbackModel` probe sent native request parameters to a native-capable primary, forced an availability failure, then reached a prompted-only fallback. The primary entered `request` with `output_mode=native`; the fallback failed in `prepare_request` with `UserError: Native structured output is not supported by this model`. Installed `fallback.py:213-265` accepts one `model_settings` and one `model_request_parameters` object for the whole loop. Therefore simply reading capabilities later does not create per-attempt request shaping; the redesign needs an explicit orchestration seam or candidate adapter.
5. **The “direct Anthropic is incapable” alternative is now rejected.** A minimal live call using the provisioned non-interactive credential and `NativeOutput` against `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` succeeded (`{ok: true}`, finish `stop`). The stronger control with `anthropic_thinking={type: enabled, budget_tokens: 1024}` also succeeded and returned one thinking part. No key value was read or printed. The current false capability is therefore an intentionally fail-closed, not-yet-recorded fact, not current provider inability.

### Legitimacy

Classification: **`intended-behavior`** for the current whole-chain intersection; the requested per-attempt resolution is an **approved superseding design change**, not restoration of the original feature. Authority:

- `worthless-titanite-bubblefish`: whole-chain conservative intersection is a settled decision and AC.
- `bixbite-sealbrown-kinkajou`: mixed chains must collapse; direct Anthropic remains unmeasured/fail-closed.
- `disparaged-gratuitous-rooster`: production bot explicitly uses Bedrock with no direct-Anthropic fallback (production scope).
- This ticket’s later operator decision and the current user direction approve replacing that policy with per-attempt capability resolution and enabling direct Anthropic locally/in CI. That approval supersedes the prior design but does not make the prior implementation a bug.

### Disposition

Do not weaken the existing intersection tests as a bug fix. Treat this ticket as the approved design-change vehicle: specify how a fallback attempt rebuilds output mode, provider-specific cache settings, sampling withdrawals, tools, and provenance when `FallbackModel` exposes only one request shape. The live direct-Anthropic native+thinking result can support a separate measured exact-id capability row, but that alone does not implement the requested general per-attempt policy. No RED contract is supplied because Phase 2 bug repair is not legitimately unlocked.

Direct Anthropic fallback should be enabled by configuring the Anthropic arm on each applicable class. The exact direct Anthropic Sonnet model has now been live-proven to support native structured output and thinking, so the earlier standard-class capability asymmetry can be resolved by recording that measured exact-ID capability; a general per-attempt workflow-routing redesign is not required for this symmetric fallback. The remaining implementation is class fallback configuration, pinned capability metadata, and a valid non-interactive credential. compiled_state.description:
## Enable the approved direct-Anthropic fallback arm in `rebar.toml`

Split out of [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882], where the operator APPROVED direct Anthropic as a
fallback arm. 2876 fixed the routing defect that made the arm appear broken (the LLM config table
was discovered from the ambient cwd rather than the gate's pinned code root, so class-routed
calls silently used the built-in bare-Anthropic defaults and 401'd). It deliberately did NOT turn
the `fallback` chain on, because doing so was MEASURED to have two blockers that are decisions in
their own right, not bug fixes.

### Blocker 1 — a chain downgrades structured output project-wide (measured)

`runner.py:441` resolves a chain's capabilities as the CONSERVATIVE INTERSECTION across its
candidates (`_intersect_capabilities`). `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` is MEASURED
native-structured-output-capable ([rebar:18ae], from a Converse PASS) while its direct-Anthropic
twin `claude-sonnet-4-6` DELIBERATELY stays PromptedOutput (`capabilities._REBAR_OVERRIDES`,
"Do not reintroduce it"). So adding the arm moves EVERY standard-class call from NativeOutput to
PromptedOutput — undoing 18ae's measured decision as a side effect of a resilience change.

MEASURED on this ticket: adding `fallback = [{ model = "claude-sonnet-4-6", provider = "anthropic" }]`
to the `standard` class fails `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py`:

    test_the_native_output_capability_difference_is_measured_and_id_scoped
    assert (True, True) == (True, False)      # the Bedrock arm started appending the prompted directive

Removing the chain returns the file to 28 passed / 0 failed. The parity suite is the guard; it
works, and it says no.

### Blocker 2 — the credential does not currently work

The `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` on the development host IS set (108 chars, `sk-ant-` prefix) and is
REJECTED by Anthropic:

    GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models  ->  HTTP 401
    {"type":"authentication_error","message":"API key is invalid."}

Enabling an arm whose key 401s buys no redundancy: it converts a legible Bedrock error into a
misleading auth error. Note also that `should_fall_back` deliberately excludes credential failures
(`CHANGE_SETTINGS`), so the chain can never rescue a bad key — the key must simply be valid.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a VALID `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is provisioned for local/CI operation (operator action — this
      cannot be done from inside a coding session) and verified with the one-line probe in
      `docs/local-dev-env.md`
- [ ] the capability-intersection consequence is resolved rather than absorbed: either the
      direct-Anthropic sonnet id is measured and enabled for native output (repeating 18ae's
      Converse measurement on the direct arm), or the chain is scoped to the classes where the
      intersection is provably lossless (frontier/opus is symmetric today), or 18ae's owner
      explicitly accepts the downgrade with a recorded rationale
- [ ] `rebar.toml` gains the `fallback` entries and the inline note explaining the blockers is
      replaced by the decision that cleared them
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` passes UNCHANGED (it must not be relaxed to
      accommodate the chain — it is the guard that caught this)
- [ ] a two-sided pin ties the fallback ids to `.github/llm-providers/anthropic.toml`, matching
      how the Bedrock ids are pinned to the bedrock overlay

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py tests/unit/test_project_default_provider.py \
           tests/unit/test_llm_config_gate_root.py tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py -q
